name: Khans of Tarkir
credit: The five clans as Wizards of the Coast's Khans of Tarkir Prerelease Primer describes them; clan cards are each clan's gold commons and uncommons. Players' notes, key cards and the two-color decks from Draftsim's Khans of Tarkir guide (2024) and MTG Arena Zone's draft guide, reworded.
about: A slow, three-color wedge format built around morph. Most good morphs cost five or more to turn face up. Fixing decides decks: players take relevant dual and tri-lands over most commons and aim for eight or more sources of each main color, three or four for a splash. Prioritize bombs and splash them when you can. Play 17 or 18 lands. The two-color decks that work are mostly enemy pairs.

src.t: Khans of Tarkir Prerelease Primer (Wizards of the Coast)
Khans of Tarkir draft guide (MTG Arena Zone)

list.d: Endurance. Outlast grows your creatures over time: hold the early game and take over the late game.
list.p: Stack the outlast lords that reward creatures with +1/+1 counters in a midrange deck. The premium removal is at uncommon. Abzan's gold cards are among the set's best.

list.d: Nimble and cunning. Prowess pumps your creatures whenever you cast a noncreature spell, so opponents hesitate to block.
list.p: Straight Jeskai is aggressive: fliers plus Arrow Storm. Jeskai Windscout is an excellent common.

list.d: Wealthy and ruthless. Delve exiles your graveyard to cast big threats early.
list.p: A grindy graveyard deck; fliers like Sultai Scavenger give it inevitability. Watch your library in long games. Its gold cards are weaker than the other clans'.

list.d: Fast, brutal and relentless. Raid rewards you for having attacked this turn.
list.p: The most aggressive clan, built to go wide. It is rarely a slow good-stuff deck.

list.d: Savage. Ferocious rewards you for controlling a creature with power 4 or greater.
list.p: Fit in as many 4-power creatures as you can. Struggles from behind but can be unstoppable after a smooth start. Woolly Loxodon is one of the best common morphs.

list.d: A players' deck: a lean curve of Warriors and their lords, sometimes with a touch of red.
list.p: One of the best archetypes. Flood the board early and pick up the two Chiefs. Plays as few as 16 lands.

list.d: A players' deck: fast aggro that punishes opponents stuck on taplands and morphs.
A players' deck built around morph payoffs and the cards that reveal themselves when turned face up.
